title: Morning-after contrarian pass — Kate Gill
content:
Quick morning-after pass on the candidate (senior runtime engineer loop). I did a contrarian read to highlight low-signal consensus areas and outline concrete follow-ups. Mostly raw — notes to self + things to land before panel vote.

High-level gut: liked their systems thinking; nervous about debugging depth with opaque GPU kernels. Strong at orchestration and policy design, weaker on low-level kernel/compilation tradeoffs. Good communicator, pragmatic about tradeoffs, but occasionally quick to generalize from limited experiments.

Observed positives:
- Thoughtful cost/latency framing — immediately asked about batching vs KV-caching tradeoffs for 99th pctl latency. Good sign for product-oriented eng.
- Clear design for canary rollouts and gradual weight migration (A/B + automatic fallback). Diagram sketch in whiteboard was concise.
- Comfortable with infra primitives: autoscaling, capacity planning, SLOs, and has runbooks for incident triage.

Risks / red flags (contrarian focus):
- Kernel-level debugging: when probed on quantization-induced accuracy drift they deferred to model/devs and did not sketch how they'd instrument or reproduce micro-biases in a perf environment. For a runtime lead we want a clear debug playbook (e.g., micro-bench harness, numerical diff suite, controlled synthetic data).
- Assumed deterministic perf from compilers (e.g., \"just pick the right kernel\"). Inference world has lots of non-determinism (memory fragmentation, multi-tenant jitter). Need examples of past incidents and mitigations.
- KV cache consistency: they proposed aggressive prefix caching but didn't articulate eviction safety under trimmed requests or model upgrades. Failure modes here can leak data or serve stale completions.

Specific technical probes to validate before deciding:
1) Give a terse kernel puzzle: small LLM forward perf regression after a compiler upgrade — ask candidate to outline immediate triage steps (tools, metrics, isolations). Look for specific metrics (token/sec, GPU SM occupancy, memcpy times, kernel launch delays), and mention of deterministic regression harness.
2) Ask for a short pseudo-code for prefix-preserving eviction with versioned cache keys — want correctness under concurrent writes and partial KV invalidation.
3) Scenario: quantized 4-bit variant shows rare hallucination spikes on a narrow prompt family. Ask for hypothesis tree + lightweight eval design to point to quantization or prompt interaction.

Behavioral / org fit notes:
- Collaborative, asked good clarifying Qs when product asked for cost targets.
- Seemed comfortable escalating and aligning with product to trade latency vs cost.
- Willingness to write docs (said they'd own runbook updates post-rollout) — positive for knowledge transfer.

Scorecard sketch (quick):
- Systems design / architecture: 8/10
- Low-level kernel & numerical debugging: 5.5/10 (major gap for deep runtime role)
- Incident response & runbooks: 8/10
- Communication & cross-team: 8.5/10
- Role fit (senior runtime lead): 6.5/10 — good on surface, gap on kernel debugging and quantization investigations.

Hiring recommendation (contrarian lens):
- If role is mostly orchestration, rollout, and API-level guarantees (Dedicated/Private), likely a good hire. We get strong product-minded runtime leadership.
- If role must own kernel-level debugging, compiler selection, and low-level perf regressions a lot of the time, this candidate would need a strong IC partner or coaching plan.

Suggested follow-ups / experiment to reduce uncertainty:
- 30-min follow-up focused only on kernel regression triage (use probe #1). Done asynchronously (take-home) or quick follow-up call.
- Ask for a short write-up (1–2 pages) on how they'd instrument a canary for a model/quantization change (cover metrics, guardrails, rollback criteria). Look for specifics (SLO thresholds, perf deltas, blackbox vs whitebox checks).

Notes to self (meta):
- Flag for interviewers to avoid accepting high-level \"we'd just\" answers. Push for concrete steps/tools.
- Balance: don't over-index on kernel debugging if the hiring funnel bottoms for orchestration leads. But document gap clearly in hiring packet.

Bottom line sentence to include on panel sheet: \"Strong orchestration and rollout instincts; borderline on low-level kernel/numerical debugging — recommend targeted follow-up to validate depth before final offer for a kernel-heavy remit.\"

Random scribbles / potential probes:
- \"How to detect K80-ish memory fragmentation on MIGs?\" (look for nvml metrics, cuda mem stats, dmesg knobs).
- \"Define a stable unit test for quantized 4-bit output equality that tolerates tiny numeric differences but catches catastrophic semantic shifts.\"

End of morning-after pass. Will draft a 1-paragraph summary for the panel Slack thread later.

-- kate
